questions.question: Which of these observations is a characteristic sign that a chemical reaction has occurred?
options: The substance changes state from solid to liquid
There is a change in colour, bubbling, or a change of temperature
The volume of a liquid decreases due to evaporation
A solid dissolves completely in water

questions.question: What is happening when you see bubbles appearing during a chemical reaction?
options: The liquid reactant is boiling
Air is being trapped from the room
A gas is being produced
The mixture is cooling down rapidly

questions.question: During a chemical reaction, what happens to the atoms of the reactants?
options: They are destroyed to make room for new elements
They rearrange themselves to form new substances
They remain in the exact same structure but change colour
They turn into energy and disappear

questions.question: Which statement generally describes the reversibility of chemical reactions?
options: Chemical reactions are easily reversed by physical means
Chemical reactions are irreversible
Chemical reactions can only be reversed by freezing
Chemical reactions are always reversible if you add water

questions.question: What three things are required for combustion to start?
options: Carbon dioxide, water, and heat
Fuel, oxygen, and an initial source of energy like heat
Nitrogen, fuel, and a cooling agent
Hydrogen, helium, and a spark

questions.question: If oxygen and carbon atoms are present in the reactants, which gas is often formed during the reaction?
options: Carbon dioxide
Hydrogen
Sulfur dioxide
Nitrogen

questions.question: What occurs during a decomposition reaction?
options: Two different elements combine to form a single compound
A single compound breaks down into two or more products
An acid and an alkali react to form a neutral solution
A solid substance dissolves completely in a liquid solvent

questions.question: When metal carbonates are heated and undergo decomposition, what products are typically formed?
options: Metal oxides and carbon dioxide gas
Metal hydroxides and oxygen gas
Pure metals and hydrogen gas
Metal chlorides and water vapour

questions.question: What term is used to describe a reaction where a substance combines with oxygen?
options: Reduction
Decomposition
Oxidation
Neutralisation

questions.question: Which of the following are both examples of oxidation reactions?
options: Combustion and rusting
Melting and evaporating
Neutralisation and filtration
Decomposition and dissolving

questions.question: Under what conditions does a precipitation reaction occur?
options: When a liquid boils and turns into a gas
When two solutions combine to form an insoluble solid
When a solid dissolves completely in water
When a gas condenses into a liquid

questions.question: How is the appearance of a precipitate used as evidence in chemistry?
options: It shows that the reaction has reached boiling point
It proves that all reactants have evaporated
It is evidence that a chemical reaction has occurred
It indicates that the reaction has absorbed heat from the surroundings

questions.question: Why are precipitation reactions useful in water treatment processes?
options: They help to dissolve large rocks in the water supply
They remove unwanted substances from water by forming insoluble solids
They add oxygen bubbles to make the water taste better
They raise the temperature of the water to kill bacteria

questions.question: In a chemical reaction, how does the mass of the products compare to the mass of the reactants?
options: The mass of the products is always greater than the mass of the reactants
The mass of the products is always less than the mass of the reactants
The mass of the products is the same as the mass of the reactants
The mass of the products depends on whether the reaction was fast or slow

questions.question: What is represented by a chemical equation?
options: How the atoms in the reactants rearrange to form the products
The time taken for the reactants to change state
The physical appearance and colour of the reactants
The volume of gas produced during a reaction

questions.question: What is the meaning of the arrow in a chemical equation?
options: It indicates that the reaction is reversible
It represents the words 'changes into'
It shows that the reaction requires cooling
It represents the words 'dissolves in'
